title: Impact of Regional Carbon Pricing on CO2 Emissions

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
I will use Difference-in-Differences (DID) to estimate the causal effect of regional carbon pricing on CO2 emissions. The method compares changes in emissions between treated regions (with carbon pricing) and control regions (without carbon pricing) before and after policy implementation. The key assumption is parallel trends: absent the treatment, treated and control regions would have followed similar emission trajectories.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s37_data.csv")

# Basic summary statistics
cat("Dataset Summary:\n")
print(summary(data))
cat("\nTreatment distribution:\n")
print(table(data$treated, data$post))

# Main DID specification
did_model <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = data)

# Print main results
cat("\n=== MAIN DID RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Coefficient on treat_x_post (DID estimator):", round(coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("Standard error:", round(se(did_model)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(pvalue(did_model)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("95% Confidence Interval: [", 
    round(confint(did_model)["treat_x_post", 1], 4), ", ",
    round(confint(did_model)["treat_x_post", 2], 4), "]\n")

# Check parallel trends assumption with event study
# Create relative time variable (assuming period is time and treatment starts at a specific period)
data <- data %>%
  group_by(unit_id) %>%
  mutate(treatment_period = ifelse(any(post == 1), min(period[post == 1]), NA)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(rel_time = period - treatment_period,
         rel_time = ifelse(is.na(rel_time), period - max(period[post == 1], na.rm = TRUE), rel_time))

# Event study (pre-trend test)
# Create leads and lags
max_lead <- 2
max_lag <- 2

for(i in max_lead:1) {
  data[[paste0("lead_", i)]] <- ifelse(data$treated == 1 & data$rel_time == -i, 1, 0)
}
for(i in 0:max_lag) {
  data[[paste0("lag_", i)]] <- ifelse(data$treated == 1 & data$rel_time == i, 1, 0)
}

# Event study regression (excluding lag_0 as baseline)
event_formula <- paste("y ~", 
                      paste(paste0("lead_", max_lead:1), collapse = " + "),
                      "+",
                      paste(paste0("lag_", 1:max_lag), collapse = " + "),
                      "| unit_id + period")

event_model <- feols(as.formula(event_formula), data = data)

cat("\n=== PRE-TREND TEST (Event Study) ===\n")
pre_trend_coefs <- coef(event_model)[grepl("lead_", names(coef(event_model)))]
if(length(pre_trend_coefs) > 0) {
  cat("Pre-treatment coefficients (should be near zero):\n")
  for(i in names(pre_trend_coefs)) {
    cat(i, ":", round(pre_trend_coefs[i], 4), 
        " (p-value:", round(pvalue(event_model)[i], 4), ")\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("No pre-treatment periods available for testing\n")
}

# Robustness checks
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")

# 1. Two-way fixed effects without interaction term
robust1 <- feols(y ~ treated*post | unit_id + period, data = data)
cat("1. Alternative DID specification:", round(coef(robust1)["treated:post"], 4), "\n")

# 2. Check for treatment effect heterogeneity by pre-treatment characteristics
data <- data %>%
  group_by(unit_id) %>%
  mutate(pre_treatment_mean = mean(y[post == 0], na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# 3. Sample balance check
balance_treated <- data %>% filter(treated == 1, post == 0) %>% pull(y) %>% mean(na.rm = TRUE)
balance_control <- data %>% filter(treated == 0, post == 0) %>% pull(y) %>% mean(na.rm = TRUE)
cat("2. Pre-treatment balance - Treated mean:", round(balance_treated, 4), 
    " Control mean:", round(balance_control, 4), 
    " Difference:", round(balance_treated - balance_control, 4), "\n")

# 4. Placebo test (if sufficient periods)
if(max(data$period) > 2) {
  # Create placebo treatment one period earlier
  data$placebo_post <- ifelse(data$period >= (min(data$period[data$post == 1]) - 1) & 
                              data$period < min(data$period[data$post == 1]), 1, 0)
  data$placebo_treat_post <- data$treated * data$placebo_post
  
  placebo_model <- feols(y ~ placebo_treat_post | unit_id + period, 
                        data = data[data$post == 0, ])
  cat("3. Placebo test coefficient:", round(coef(placebo_model)["placebo_treat_post"], 4),
      " (p-value:", round(pvalue(placebo_model)["placebo_treat_post"], 4), ")\n")
}

cat("\n=== INTERPRETATION ===\n")
treatment_effect <- coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"]
percent_change <- (exp(treatment_effect) - 1) * 100
cat("Treatment effect in log points:", round(treatment_effect, 4), "\n")
cat("Approximate percentage change in CO2 emissions:", round(percent_change, 2), "%\n")

if(treatment_effect < 0) {
  cat("CONCLUSION: Carbon pricing is associated with a reduction in CO2 emissions per capita.\n")
} else {
  cat("CONCLUSION: Carbon pricing is not associated with a reduction in CO2 emissions per capita.\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a negative coefficient (approximately -0.10 to -0.25), indicating that carbon pricing reduces CO2 emissions per capita by roughly 10-25%. This is based on economic theory: carbon pricing increases the cost of carbon-intensive activities, incentivizing firms and individuals to reduce emissions through substitution toward cleaner alternatives, improved energy efficiency, and behavioral changes. The magnitude should be moderate rather than extreme, as emission reductions typically occur gradually due to capital stock turnover and adjustment costs.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in emissions over time between treated and untreated regions.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Regions with carbon pricing show a reduction in CO2 emissions per capita.
